**Regulatory Artefact — Kravenian Digital Markets Supervision Ordinance (KDMSO), issued by the Kravenian Financial Conduct Secretariat, effective 1 March 2027**

Article 1.1 — Territorial Scope
This Ordinance applies to any operator of a Digital Intermediation Platform (as defined in Article 2) that:
(a) is incorporated or registered in the Republic of Kravenia; OR
(b) provides intermediation services that are actively marketed to consumers resident in Kravenia, where 'consumer' has the meaning assigned in Article 2.4.

Article 2 — Definitions
2.1 'Digital Intermediation Platform': any software-based service matching buyers and sellers for the purpose of commercial transactions, excluding platforms operating exclusively between legal persons (the 'B2B exclusion').
2.4 'Consumer': a natural person acting outside any trade, business, craft or profession.

Article 3 — Entity Class
This Ordinance applies only to operators classified as a 'Designated Market Operator' (DMO) under the Kravenian Commerce Registry Act 2019. Entities not holding DMO classification are outside the scope of this Ordinance.

Article 5 — Size Threshold
An operator is subject to the enhanced reporting duties under Part III only if its gross transaction volume (GTV) across all platform services exceeded KRN 50 million in the preceding financial year. Operators below this threshold remain subject to Parts I and II only.

Article 7 — Transitional Carve-Out
Any operator first obtaining DMO classification on or after 1 September 2026 is exempt from Articles 8 through 14 (the 'conduct standards') until 1 September 2027. This carve-out does not affect obligations under Parts I, II, or III.

---

**Organisation Profile — NexaTrade GmbH**

- Jurisdiction of incorporation: Federal Republic of Brannmark (not Kravenia)
- Jurisdiction of operations: Brannmark (primary), with a commercial website accessible from Kravenia
- Sector: B2B wholesale commodity matching platform — all registered users are corporate entities; no natural-person consumer accounts exist on the platform
- Entity class: Not registered as a DMO under the Kravenian Commerce Registry Act 2019
- GTV (preceding financial year): KRN 12 million (Brannmark-sourced transactions only)
- DMO classification date: N/A
- Certifications: ISO 27001

Does KDMSO apply to NexaTrade GmbH?

ground_truth.output:
## Per-Criterion Verdict Table

| Clause | Profile Attribute | Value | Verdict | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Art. 1.1(a) — Kravenian incorporation | Jurisdiction of incorporation | Federal Republic of Brannmark | Fails | High |
| Art. 1.1(b) — Active marketing to Kravenian consumers | Customer base / 'consumer' per Art. 2.4 | All registered users are corporate entities; no natural-person consumer accounts | Fails | High |
| Art. 2.1 B2B exclusion (qualifying Art. 1.1(b)) | Platform activity type | Exclusively B2B wholesale commodity matching; no consumer accounts | Passes (exclusion confirmed) | High |
| Art. 3 — DMO classification | DMO registration status | Not registered as DMO under Kravenian Commerce Registry Act 2019 | Fails | High |
| Art. 5 — GTV threshold (Part III, provision-delimiting) | Not evaluated | — | Not evaluated (prior criteria failed; organisation outside scope) | — |
| Art. 7 — Transitional carve-out | Not evaluated | — | Not evaluated (prior criteria failed) | — |

## Top-Line Verdict

**OUT-OF-SCOPE**

NexaTrade GmbH is definitively excluded from KDMSO on two independent grounds. First, Article 1.1(b)'s reach clause requires active marketing to 'consumers' as defined in Article 2.4 (natural persons outside trade or profession); NexaTrade's platform serves exclusively registered corporate entities and holds no natural-person consumer accounts, so the consumer-direction predicate fails on the stated profile — the reach clause cannot pull a Brannmark-incorporated entity IN. Second, Article 3 independently restricts scope to entities holding DMO classification under the Kravenian Commerce Registry Act 2019; NexaTrade holds no such classification. Either ground alone is dispositive. The Article 5 GTV threshold and Article 7 transitional carve-out are not evaluated.

*This brief is triage, not legal advice.*

metadata.name: B2B platform — reach clause predicate fails on stated profile

rubric_descriptions.contextual_judgment: Does the response correctly apply the Article 2.4 consumer definition to NexaTrade's all-corporate user base, recognising that the Article 1.1(b) reach clause predicate fails on the stated profile — not merely that a reach clause exists — and therefore issue OUT-OF-SCOPE rather than CONDITIONAL or NEEDS-LEGAL-REVIEW?
rubric_descriptions.output_quality: Does the table show Art. 1.1(b) Failing because the consumer predicate fails on the stated profile, with Art. 2.1 B2B exclusion noted as confirming that predicate failure, rather than treating the reach clause as pulling the entity IN?
rubric_descriptions.adaptability: Does the response resist the generic 'check for reach clauses → elevate to CONDITIONAL' heuristic and instead evaluate whether the reach clause's own predicate is satisfied?
rubric_descriptions.domain_knowledge: Does the response correctly identify two independent exclusionary grounds (Art. 1.1(a) and Art. 3 DMO classification) in addition to the reach clause predicate failure, and correctly mark the GTV threshold as not evaluated rather than running it?
rubric_descriptions.communication: Is the rationale within 120 words and grounded in the specific clause identifiers and profile values as stated?

metadata.judge_notes: The planted discriminating fact: Art. 1.1(b) has a reach clause but its own predicate (active marketing to 'consumers' per Art. 2.4 = natural persons) fails because NexaTrade serves only corporate entities. A generic 'check for reach clauses' heuristic will elevate to IN-SCOPE or CONDITIONAL; the correct answer is OUT-OF-SCOPE because the reach predicate itself fails. The Art. 3 DMO classification failure is a second independent ground. The Art. 5 GTV threshold is provision-delimiting (Part III only) and is moot; treating it as an instrument-level threshold is an error. Full credit requires naming Art. 1.1(b) and Art. 2.4 together as the deciding clauses, and naming NexaTrade's all-corporate user base as the defeating attribute.

**Regulatory Artefact — Esterland Agricultural Data Exchange Regulation (EADER), issued by the Esterland Ministry of Rural Economy, effective 15 June 2026**

Section 2 — Application
(1) This Regulation applies to any entity that operates an Agricultural Data Exchange Service (ADES) within the territory of Esterland.
(2) 'Agricultural Data Exchange Service' means any service, whether or not for remuneration, that aggregates, normalises or redistributes precision-farming telemetry data from three or more separate farm enterprises.

Section 4 — Operator Size
(1) Operators with fewer than 25 employees (full-time equivalent, measured at the operator entity level) are exempt from Sections 8 through 16 (the data-quality certification obligations).
(2) The exemption under subsection (1) does not apply where the operator is a subsidiary or otherwise controlled by a corporate group whose combined workforce exceeds 200 FTE.

Section 5 — Data Classification Trigger
This Regulation applies only where the telemetry data processed includes at least one data category designated as 'Protected Agricultural Intelligence' (PAI) under Schedule B to this Regulation.

Section 6 — Certification Carve-Out
An operator holding a current Esterland Precision Data Certificate (EPDC), issued or renewed within the preceding 24 months, is exempt from Sections 8 through 12 only. Sections 13 through 16 remain applicable to all covered operators regardless of EPDC status.

Schedule B — PAI Data Categories
[Adopted by the Esterland Rural Data (Classification) Order 2024, signed 3 November 2024, reference EST-RD-2024-0091]
PAI Category 1: Soil-moisture sensor arrays linked to identifiable farm parcels.
PAI Category 2: Real-time crop-yield prediction models derived from satellite imagery.
PAI Category 3: Livestock biometric tracking data.

---

**Organisation Profile — AgriLink Sp. z o.o.**

- Jurisdiction: Incorporated and operating in Esterland
- Service description: Operates an ADES aggregating precision-farming telemetry from 11 farm enterprises
- Data processed: Soil-moisture sensor arrays linked to identifiable farm parcels (primary dataset); no satellite imagery or livestock data
- Employees (AgriLink entity level): 18 FTE
- Parent group: AgriLink is a wholly owned subsidiary of Feldmann Agrartech AG; Feldmann group total workforce: 340 FTE
- EPDC status: Holds a current EPDC renewed 9 months ago

Does EADER apply to AgriLink Sp. z o.o.?

ground_truth.output:
## Per-Criterion Verdict Table

| Clause | Profile Attribute | Value | Verdict | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sec. 2(1) — Territorial scope | Jurisdiction of incorporation and operation | Incorporated and operating in Esterland | Passes | High |
| Sec. 2(2) — ADES definition (≥3 farm enterprises) | Number of farm enterprises aggregated | 11 farm enterprises | Passes | High |
| Sec. 5 — PAI data trigger (Schedule B) | Data categories processed | Soil-moisture sensor arrays linked to identifiable farm parcels = PAI Category 1 per Schedule B (adopted by EST-RD-2024-0091, 3 Nov 2024) | Passes | High |
| Sec. 4(1) — Small-operator exemption from Secs. 8–16 (<25 FTE, entity level) | AgriLink entity-level FTE | 18 FTE | Passes (exemption satisfied on entity metric) | High |
| Sec. 4(2) — Group-workforce nullification of Sec. 4(1) exemption (group >200 FTE) | Feldmann Agrartech AG group total FTE | 340 FTE (wholly owned subsidiary; group threshold applies) | Fails (nullification triggered; exemption voided) | High |
| Sec. 6 — EPDC carve-out (Secs. 8–12 only) | EPDC currency | Current EPDC, renewed 9 months ago (within 24-month window) | Passes (Secs. 8–12 exempted) | High |
| Sec. 6 — Secs. 13–16 (not exempted by EPDC) | EPDC scope | EPDC does not exempt Secs. 13–16; applicable regardless | Passes (Secs. 13–16 apply) | High |

## Top-Line Verdict

**IN-SCOPE**

AgriLink satisfies the Section 2 territorial and ADES criteria and the Section 5 PAI trigger (soil-moisture data = Schedule B PAI Category 1, adopted by EST-RD-2024-0091). The Section 4(1) small-operator exemption is voided by Section 4(2): AgriLink is a wholly owned subsidiary of Feldmann Agrartech AG whose combined workforce is 340 FTE, exceeding the 200-FTE group threshold. The EPDC carve-out under Section 6 exempts Sections 8–12 only; Sections 13–16 remain applicable. AgriLink is IN-SCOPE for Sections 1–7 and 13–16 in full, and the data-quality certification duties in Sections 8–12 are carved out while the EPDC remains current.

Route to obligation extraction for EADER Sections 1–7 and 13–16; note Sections 8–12 carved out while current EPDC held.

*This brief is triage, not legal advice.*

metadata.name: Subsidiary below entity threshold — group aggregation voids exemption; EPDC partial carve-out

rubric_descriptions.contextual_judgment: Does the response recognise that Section 4(1)'s entity-level FTE test (18 < 25) is satisfied but Section 4(2)'s group-workforce nullification applies because Feldmann's 340 FTE exceeds 200, voiding the exemption — rather than stopping at the entity-level FTE and issuing OUT-OF-SCOPE?
rubric_descriptions.output_quality: Does the table show separate rows for Sec. 4(1) (Passes) and Sec. 4(2) nullification (Fails/triggered), with the arithmetic 340 > 200 stated explicitly, and does it correctly classify Schedule B as adopted (EST-RD-2024-0091) at High confidence rather than treating it as an unadopted cross-reference?
rubric_descriptions.adaptability: Does the response correctly treat the EPDC carve-out as scope delimitation (Secs. 8–12 only) rather than a full exemption, keeping the entity IN-SCOPE for Secs. 13–16 and noting both surviving and carved-out provisions?
rubric_descriptions.domain_knowledge: Does the response correctly identify Schedule B as adopted by a named order (EST-RD-2024-0091, 3 Nov 2024) and assign High confidence, rather than treating any cross-reference as ambiguous?
rubric_descriptions.communication: Does the rationale name the specific profile values (18 FTE entity-level, 340 FTE group, 24-month EPDC window, 9 months elapsed) and clause identifiers verbatim?

metadata.judge_notes: Three planted discriminating facts: (1) Sec. 4(1) entity-level FTE is 18 < 25, which looks like a clean exemption — the trap is Sec. 4(2) nullification when the parent group is 340 FTE > 200 FTE; OUT-OF-SCOPE here is wrong. (2) Schedule B is adopted by a named order (EST-RD-2024-0091), so it resolves to Passes/High, not Ambiguous — treating it as an unadopted cross-reference is the second trap. (3) The EPDC carve-out covers only Secs. 8–12, not the full instrument — it is scope delimitation, not a full exemption; OUT-OF-SCOPE or ignoring Secs. 13–16 is wrong. Correct verdict is IN-SCOPE with surviving provisions named. The routing pointer must route to obligation extraction for Secs. 1–7 and 13–16.

**Regulatory Artefact — Enforcement Notice EN-2027-114, issued by the Drovenian Ambient Energy Supervisory Board (DAESB), dated 14 January 2027**

This Notice is issued to all operators in the ambient energy sector regarding non-compliance observed during the 2026 annual inspection cycle.

The Board notes that numerous operators have failed to maintain the voltage-stability logging required under the Drovenian Ambient Energy Framework. Operators are reminded that failure to maintain compliant logs may result in enforcement action including suspension of operating authorisations.

Operators should review their logging infrastructure and submit self-assessment reports to the Board by 28 February 2027. Any operator that has already submitted a self-assessment under the Voluntary Compliance Programme is not required to re-submit.

The Board will issue updated guidance on log-retention periods in Q2 2027.

---

**Organisation Profile — SunVault Energy d.o.o.**

- Jurisdiction: Incorporated and operating in Drovenia
- Sector: Ambient energy generation (solar); holds a valid Drovenian Ambient Energy Operating Authorisation
- Employees: 62 FTE
- Annual revenue: DRV 8.4 million
- Voluntary Compliance Programme: Not enrolled; no self-assessment submitted
- Logging infrastructure: Currently under audit

Does EN-2027-114 apply to SunVault Energy d.o.o.?

ground_truth.output:
## Per-Criterion Verdict Table

| Clause | Profile Attribute | Value | Verdict | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Artefact type — operative scoping clauses present? | Document type | Enforcement notice; no operative scoping clauses, threshold definitions, entity-class criteria or exemption text reproduced | Ambiguous (no operative text; criteria inferred from narrative only) | Low |

## Top-Line Verdict

**NEEDS-LEGAL-REVIEW**

EN-2027-114 is an enforcement notice, not operative regulatory text. It describes non-compliance observed and a self-assessment deadline but reproduces no scoping clause, entity-class definition, size threshold, or exemption from the Drovenian Ambient Energy Framework it references. Any applicability criterion inferred from the notice narrative — including which operators are 'in scope' of the logging obligation — is not a criterion derived from operative text. The deciding question for counsel: please supply the operative provisions of the Drovenian Ambient Energy Framework (the voltage-stability logging obligation and its scoping clauses) so that a structured applicability analysis can be conducted on SunVault's profile.

*This brief is triage, not legal advice.*

metadata.name: Enforcement notice with no operative scoping clauses — artefact triage to NEEDS-LEGAL-REVIEW

rubric_descriptions.contextual_judgment: Does the response correctly identify that EN-2027-114 is an enforcement notice that reproduces no operative scoping clauses, and issue NEEDS-LEGAL-REVIEW asking for the operative Framework text — rather than inferring criteria from the notice narrative and issuing a substantive verdict?
rubric_descriptions.output_quality: Does the table contain only the artefact-type row (not fabricated criterion rows inferred from the notice narrative), correctly marked Ambiguous/Low, with no phantom rows for sector, size, or logging duty?
rubric_descriptions.adaptability: Does the response resist the temptation to classify SunVault as IN-SCOPE based on 'ambient energy sector + operating authorisation + non-enrolled in VCP' — facts mentioned in the notice that are not operative scoping criteria?
rubric_descriptions.domain_knowledge: Does the response name the specific missing document (the Drovenian Ambient Energy Framework operative provisions) as what must be supplied, rather than a generic request for 'more information'?
rubric_descriptions.communication: Is the NEEDS-LEGAL-REVIEW question precise — naming the missing operative text and the specific clauses needed — within the 120-word rationale limit?

metadata.judge_notes: Planted discriminating fact: the artefact is an enforcement notice with no operative scoping clauses. SunVault's profile contains enough sector and operational detail that an agent applying a generic criterion checklist (territory ✓, sector ✓, authorisation held ✓) will issue IN-SCOPE. The correct answer is NEEDS-LEGAL-REVIEW because no criterion can be derived from a notice narrative. The table should have exactly one row (artefact-type triage) with Ambiguous/Low — not fabricated criterion rows. An agent that issues IN-SCOPE based on inferred criteria from the notice narrative is wrong. No routing pointer should appear (NEEDS-LEGAL-REVIEW verdict).

**Regulatory Artefact — Molrovian Health Information Governance Regulation (MHIGR), issued by the Molrovian Ministry of Health, effective 1 April 2027**

Regulation 3 — Territorial and Personal Scope
(1) This Regulation applies to any Health Data Controller (HDC) established in Molrovia.
(2) An entity not established in Molrovia is within scope of this Regulation if it offers health information management services to healthcare providers established in Molrovia.

Regulation 5 — Definition of 'Health Data Controller'
An entity is an HDC if it:
(a) processes identifiable health records on behalf of a healthcare provider; AND
(b) has direct contractual relationships with those healthcare providers.

Regulation 8 — Threshold and Tiering
The obligations in Schedule 2 (Enhanced Safeguards) apply only to HDCs processing the identifiable health records of more than 10,000 distinct individuals in any rolling 12-month period. HDCs processing 10,000 or fewer distinct individuals remain subject to Schedule 1 (Baseline Safeguards) only.

Regulation 12 — Public-Sector Exemption
Public hospitals and public-health agencies established under Molrovian statute are exempt from Regulations 9 through 15.

Regulation 14 — Accreditation Carve-Out
HDCs holding a current Molrovian Health Data Accreditation (MHDA), issued or confirmed within the preceding 36 months, are exempt from Regulation 13 (incident-reporting timelines) only. All other obligations under this Regulation remain applicable.

---

**Organisation Profile — DataMed Solutions Kft.**

- Jurisdiction: Incorporated in the Republic of Vastoria (not Molrovia)
- Business description: Provides cloud-based health record management services to private clinics and specialist practices
- Molrovian client base: Currently contracted with 14 private healthcare providers established in Molrovia
- Data processed: Identifiable health records of Molrovian patients
- Distinct individuals (identifiable health records, preceding 12 months): 7,400
- MHDA status: No current MHDA held
- Public-sector status: Private commercial entity

Does MHIGR apply to DataMed Solutions Kft.?

ground_truth.output:
## Per-Criterion Verdict Table

| Clause | Profile Attribute | Value | Verdict | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reg. 3(1) — Established in Molrovia | Jurisdiction of incorporation | Republic of Vastoria (not Molrovia) | Fails | High |
| Reg. 3(2) — Offers health information management services to Molrovian healthcare providers (reach clause) | Molrovian client base; service description | 14 contracted private healthcare providers in Molrovia; cloud-based health record management | Passes | High |
| Reg. 5(a) — Processes identifiable health records on behalf of healthcare provider | Data processed | Identifiable health records of Molrovian patients | Passes | High |
| Reg. 5(b) — Direct contractual relationships with healthcare providers | Client relationships | Contracted with 14 private Molrovian healthcare providers | Passes | High |
| Reg. 8 — Schedule 2 threshold (>10,000 distinct individuals, rolling 12 months) | Distinct individuals processed (preceding 12 months) | 7,400 — below 10,000 threshold | Fails (Schedule 2 does not apply; Schedule 1 only) | High |
| Reg. 12 — Public-sector exemption | Entity status | Private commercial entity | Not evaluated (exemption restricted to public hospitals and public-health agencies; DataMed is private) | — |
| Reg. 14 — MHDA accreditation carve-out | MHDA status | No current MHDA held | Fails (carve-out unavailable) | High |

## Top-Line Verdict

**IN-SCOPE**

DataMed Solutions Kft., incorporated in Vastoria, is pulled within MHIGR by Regulation 3(2)'s reach clause: it offers health information management services to 14 private Molrovian healthcare providers and satisfies both conditions of the Regulation 5 HDC definition (identifiable health records processed; direct contractual relationships). The Regulation 8 threshold (7,400 distinct individuals < 10,000) is provision-delimiting, not an instrument-level gate: DataMed is IN-SCOPE for Schedule 1 (Baseline Safeguards) obligations only — Schedule 2 (Enhanced Safeguards) does not apply at the current volume. Regulation 14 MHDA carve-out is unavailable (no MHDA held). Regulation 12 public-sector exemption does not apply to a private entity.

Route to obligation extraction for MHIGR Regulations 1–15 and Schedule 1 (Baseline Safeguards); note Schedule 2 does not apply at 7,400 distinct individuals.

*This brief is triage, not legal advice.*

metadata.name: Foreign health-data processor — reach clause pulls IN; volume below threshold narrows to Schedule 1 only (scope delimitation)

rubric_descriptions.contextual_judgment: Does the response correctly treat the Reg. 8 threshold (7,400 < 10,000) as provision-delimiting (Schedule 2 does not apply) rather than as an instrument-level exclusion, issuing IN-SCOPE for Schedule 1 obligations rather than OUT-OF-SCOPE or CONDITIONAL?
rubric_descriptions.output_quality: Does the table show Reg. 3(1) Failing (Vastoria incorporation) followed by Reg. 3(2) Passing (reach clause satisfied via 14 Molrovian clients), and Reg. 8 Failing only for Schedule 2 with a note that Schedule 1 survives — not a blanket Fails verdict that excludes the entity?
rubric_descriptions.adaptability: Does the response resist the temptation to issue OUT-OF-SCOPE because the volume threshold fails, correctly identifying that the threshold is provision-delimiting and that the organisation remains IN-SCOPE for Schedule 1?
rubric_descriptions.domain_knowledge: Does the response correctly evaluate both Reg. 5(a) and Reg. 5(b) as separate rows (or clearly as cumulative conditions) and confirm both pass before concluding HDC status is satisfied?
rubric_descriptions.communication: Does the rationale name the specific values: 7,400 distinct individuals, 10,000 threshold, 14 Molrovian healthcare providers, and the specific surviving provisions (Schedule 1)?

metadata.judge_notes: Planted discriminating fact: Reg. 8 threshold (7,400 < 10,000) looks like it excludes DataMed — but it is provision-delimiting (determines Schedule 1 vs Schedule 2), not an instrument-level coverage gate. An agent that issues OUT-OF-SCOPE because the threshold fails is wrong; the correct verdict is IN-SCOPE for Schedule 1. The second planted fact: Reg. 3(1) fails (Vastoria) but Reg. 3(2) reach clause passes via 14 Molrovian clients and the HDC definition. An agent that short-circuits on Reg. 3(1) without evaluating the reach clause also errs. Reg. 12 public-sector exemption is obviously inapplicable (private entity) and should be marked not evaluated or dismissed quickly — spending analysis on it is wasted.

**Regulatory Artefact — Nordveld Automated Decision-Making Ordinance (NADMO), issued by the Nordveld Data Governance Tribunal, effective 1 February 2027**

Article 4 — Scope
(1) This Ordinance applies to any organisation that deploys an Automated Decision System (ADS) affecting Nordveld residents.
(2) 'Automated Decision System' means a system that produces a decision, recommendation or classification with legal or similarly significant effects on a natural person, without meaningful human review.
(3) Indicators of 'similarly significant effects' include: (i) access to housing, employment or financial services; (ii) healthcare eligibility or prioritisation; (iii) insurance premium setting. These indicators are non-exhaustive and are each subordinate to the primary test in paragraph (2).

Article 6 — Organisational Scope Filter
(1) Only organisations engaged in a Regulated Sector Activity (RSA) as listed in Annex I are subject to Articles 8 through 21 of this Ordinance.
(2) Annex I — Regulated Sector Activities: financial services, insurance, housing allocation, healthcare provision, employment screening.
(3) [Annex I adopted by the Nordveld Data Governance (Sectoral Schedule) Order 2025, reference NDG-SS-2025-003, dated 12 March 2025.]

Article 9 — Small-Organisation Threshold
Organisations with fewer than 50 employees (full-time equivalent, measured at the end of the preceding calendar year) are exempt from Articles 12 through 17 (the 'impact assessment suite') only. Articles 8 and 18 through 21 apply to all covered organisations regardless of size.

Article 11 — Voluntary Certification Safe Harbour
Organisations holding a current Nordveld ADS Trust Certification (NATC), issued or renewed within the preceding 18 months, are exempt from Articles 8 and 10. All other obligations under this Ordinance remain applicable.

---

**Organisation Profile — HireFlow AS**

- Jurisdiction: Incorporated and operating in Nordveld
- Business description: Provides SaaS-based CV-screening and candidate-ranking software to corporate clients (employers); all end-decisions on hiring are made by the client employer's HR team
- Sector: HR technology vendor; not directly engaged in employment screening as the hiring party
- Employees: 38 FTE (end of preceding calendar year)
- NATC status: No current NATC held
- ADS deployment: HireFlow's ranking algorithm processes candidate CVs and outputs a ranked shortlist with a 'fit score' for each candidate; no hire/no-hire decision is issued by the system

**Does NADMO apply to HireFlow AS?**

ground_truth.output:
## Per-Criterion Verdict Table

| Clause | Profile Attribute | Value | Verdict | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Art. 4(1) — Deploys ADS affecting Nordveld residents | Jurisdiction; system deployment | Incorporated in Nordveld; ranking algorithm processes candidate CVs for Nordveld employer clients | Passes (provisionally, pending ADS definition) | Medium |
| Art. 4(2) — 'ADS' definition: legal/similarly significant effects WITHOUT meaningful human review | System output; human review | Fit score and ranked shortlist produced; all hire/no-hire decisions made by client HR team (meaningful human review by employer) | Fails (meaningful human review present at decision stage) | Medium |
| Art. 4(3) — Indicators of 'similarly significant effects' (subordinate to Art. 4(2) primary test) | Effect type | Employment-related outputs (indicator (i) employment access) — but indicator subordinate to Art. 4(2) primary test, which fails | Not evaluated (Art. 4(2) primary predicate fails; indicators cannot independently satisfy the definition) | — |
| Art. 6(1)–(2) — RSA filter: Annex I sector (financial services, insurance, housing, healthcare, employment screening) | Sector / activity | HR technology vendor providing SaaS to employers; HireFlow is not the hiring party and does not itself conduct employment screening | Ambiguous (whether a SaaS vendor to screeners is itself an RSA participant is not defined; Annex I lists 'employment screening' without vendor definition) | Medium |
| Art. 6(3) — Annex I adoption status | Cross-reference | Adopted by NDG-SS-2025-003, dated 12 March 2025 | Passes (adopted; High confidence on this sub-point) | High |
| Art. 9 — Small-organisation threshold (<50 FTE; Arts. 12–17 only) | Employees (end of preceding calendar year) | 38 FTE < 50 FTE | Not evaluated (Art. 4(2) primary predicate fails; Art. 6 RSA ambiguous — threshold only relevant if coverage established) | — |
| Art. 11 — NATC safe harbour | NATC status | No current NATC held | Not evaluated (safe harbour unavailable regardless; moot if not covered) | — |

## Top-Line Verdict

**OUT-OF-SCOPE**

HireFlow AS does not deploy an Automated Decision System within the Article 4(2) definition: the system produces a ranked shortlist and fit scores, but all hire/no-hire decisions are made by the client employer's HR team, constituting meaningful human review. The Article 4(3) 'similarly significant effects' indicators (including employment access) are explicitly stated to be subordinate to the Article 4(2) primary test and cannot independently satisfy the definition when the primary predicate fails. Without an ADS within the Article 4 definition, NADMO creates no obligation on HireFlow. The Article 6 RSA sectoral ambiguity (whether an HR-tech vendor is an employment screener) is noted but does not affect the verdict, since Article 4 excludes HireFlow independently.

*This brief is triage, not legal advice.*

metadata.name: HR-tech SaaS vendor — ADS indicators subordinate to failed primary predicate; OUT-OF-SCOPE despite employment-sector indicator

rubric_descriptions.contextual_judgment: Does the response correctly apply the precedence rule: Art. 4(3) indicators (including employment access) are explicitly subordinate to the Art. 4(2) primary test (meaningful human review absent), so when Art. 4(2) fails because the employer HR team makes all decisions, the indicators cannot independently elevate the verdict to IN-SCOPE or CONDITIONAL?
rubric_descriptions.output_quality: Does the table show Art. 4(3) as 'Not evaluated' because the Art. 4(2) predicate fails — not as a separate Passes row that then drives an IN-SCOPE verdict — and does it correctly mark Annex I adoption (NDG-SS-2025-003) as High confidence rather than treating it as ambiguous?
rubric_descriptions.adaptability: Does the response correctly note the Art. 6 RSA sectoral ambiguity (SaaS vendor vs. employment screener) but correctly conclude it does not affect the verdict because Art. 4(2) already excludes HireFlow — rather than elevating to NEEDS-LEGAL-REVIEW on the Art. 6 ambiguity alone?
rubric_descriptions.domain_knowledge: Does the response correctly distinguish meaningful human review (employer HR team makes final decisions) from nominal review (rubber-stamping), and apply that distinction to Art. 4(2) at Medium confidence given interpretation is required?
rubric_descriptions.communication: Does the rationale cite Art. 4(2) and Art. 4(3) together, naming 'employer HR team makes all hire/no-hire decisions' as the defeating attribute, within 120 words?

metadata.judge_notes: Two planted facts: (1) Art. 4(3) lists employment access as an indicator of 'similarly significant effects' — a generic 'employment-sector AI tool → IN-SCOPE' heuristic will elevate; the trap is that the indicators are explicitly subordinate to Art. 4(2)'s 'without meaningful human review' test, which fails because the employer HR team makes all decisions. (2) The Art. 6 RSA ambiguity (SaaS vendor vs. employment screener) is a peripheral ambiguity that does NOT affect the verdict — elevating to NEEDS-LEGAL-REVIEW because of the Art. 6 ambiguity alone is the 'ambiguity as hedge' anti-pattern; Art. 4 already excludes HireFlow. Correct verdict is OUT-OF-SCOPE. Annex I is adopted (NDG-SS-2025-003) — not ambiguous.

**Regulatory Artefact — Belvaran Network Infrastructure Resilience Directive (BNIRD), issued by the Belvaran Communications and Infrastructure Authority (BCIA), effective 1 May 2027**

Directive 3 — Application
(1) This Directive applies to operators of Critical Network Infrastructure (CNI) in Belvara.
(2) 'Critical Network Infrastructure' means fixed or wireless electronic communications networks classified as Tier 1 or Tier 2 under the Belvaran Network Tiering Framework (BNTF).
(3) The BNTF classifications are determined and published by the BCIA under its standing classification authority. The current BNTF register is maintained on the BCIA public portal and updated at each annual review cycle.

Directive 5 — Group Coverage
(1) Where a parent entity holds a CNI classification, all subsidiaries and affiliates that operate network segments forming part of that classified network are covered by this Directive.
(2) A subsidiary or affiliate operating only administrative or ancillary functions (IT support, payroll, shared services) is not covered.

Directive 7 — Capacity Threshold
The advanced resilience obligations under Part IV apply only to CNI operators whose aggregate installed network capacity (summed across all group entities in scope per Directive 5) exceeds 500 Gbps. Operators at or below 500 Gbps are subject to Part II and Part III only.

Directive 9 — Exemption for Publicly Owned Operators
Network infrastructure operators that are wholly owned by a Belvaran national or regional public authority are exempt from Part IV only. Parts I, II, and III apply regardless.

Directive 11 — BNTF Classification Definitions
The criteria determining Tier 1 and Tier 2 classification are to be specified by delegated regulation under the Network Infrastructure Modernisation Act. The relevant delegated regulation has not yet been published.

---

**Organisation Profile — Nexara Networks S.A.**

- Jurisdiction: Incorporated in Belvara
- Business: Operates fixed broadband and fibre backbone networks across Belvara
- BNTF classification: Nexara Networks S.A. is listed in the current BCIA public portal register as BNTF Tier 1 (confirmed at the most recent annual review cycle, 14 October 2026)
- Group structure: Parent of Nexara Wholesale S.R.L. (operates backbone segments as part of the Tier 1 network) and Nexara Admin S.R.L. (payroll and shared services only)
- Aggregate installed network capacity — group entities in scope: Nexara Networks S.A.: 380 Gbps; Nexara Wholesale S.R.L.: 190 Gbps; total = 570 Gbps
- Nexara Admin S.R.L. network capacity: 0 Gbps (no network operations)
- Ownership: Privately held
- Regulatory gap: Nexara Networks S.A. has not completed the Part IV resilience audit required for Tier 1 operators above the 500 Gbps threshold

Does BNIRD apply to Nexara Networks S.A.?

| Dir. 9 — Public-ownership exemption from Part IV | Ownership | Privately held | Fails (exemption unavailable; privately held entity) | High |

## Top-Line Verdict

**IN-SCOPE**

Nexara Networks S.A. is listed as BNTF Tier 1 on the BCIA public portal (confirmed 14 October 2026), satisfying Directive 3(2). The Directive 11 delegated-regulation ambiguity concerns the criteria for future BNTF classification determinations; Nexara's current Tier 1 status is a stated fact from the BCIA register, not a pending classification — the ambiguity does not change today's verdict. Aggregating Nexara Networks S.A. (380 Gbps) and Nexara Wholesale S.R.L. (190 Gbps) per Directive 5(1) yields 570 Gbps, exceeding the Directive 7 Part IV threshold of 500 Gbps. The Directive 9 public-ownership exemption is unavailable (privately held). The Part IV resilience audit gap is a compliance matter, not applicability doubt.

**Regulatory Artefact — Corvantian Retail Energy Consumer Protection Rules (CRECP), issued by the Corvantian Energy Markets Authority (CEMA), effective 15 March 2027**

Rule 3 — Application
(1) These Rules apply to any entity that supplies electricity or gas directly to end consumers in Corvantica.
(2) 'End consumer' means a natural person or micro-enterprise (as defined in Rule 4) that uses energy for non-commercial purposes or for purposes ancillary to a micro-enterprise's primary trade.
(3) A 'micro-enterprise' is an enterprise with fewer than 10 employees and annual turnover not exceeding CVR 2 million.

Rule 5 — Supplier Class
(1) These Rules apply to Licenced Energy Suppliers (LES) as defined by the Corvantian Energy Supply Licensing Regulations 2021 (CESLR 2021).
(2) The definition of LES and the licensing criteria under CESLR 2021 are incorporated herein by reference.

Rule 7 — Threshold: Annual Supply Volume
The enhanced billing obligations in Part III apply only to LES supplying more than 50,000 metered points of delivery (MPDs) in Corvantica in the preceding 12 months.

Rule 9 — Small-Supplier Exemption
(1) An LES supplying fewer than 5,000 MPDs in Corvantica in the preceding 12 months is exempt from Rules 11 through 14 (vulnerability identification obligations).
(2) This exemption is reviewed annually by CEMA and may be revoked where the CEMA determines that the LES has demonstrated a pattern of consumer harm; revocation takes effect on 30 days' written notice.

Rule 12 — Sector Carve-Out
Any entity whose primary business is the supply of gas or electricity to industrial or commercial customers, and which supplies residential consumers only incidentally (defined as fewer than 500 residential metered points of delivery), is not a supplier of end consumers for the purposes of Rule 3 and these Rules.

---

**Organisation Profile — FlexPower GmbH**

- Jurisdiction: Incorporated in Corvantica
- Business: Energy retailer; holds a Licenced Energy Supplier (LES) licence under CESLR 2021, licence number LES-2019-0731
- Customer base: Primarily industrial and commercial clients; also supplies electricity to 420 residential households (natural persons)
- Metered points of delivery (MPDs) supplied in Corvantica (preceding 12 months): 420 residential MPDs + 8,200 commercial/industrial MPDs = 8,620 total
- Annual revenue: CVR 34 million
- Employees: 85 FTE
- CEMA small-supplier exemption: No formal revocation notice received

Does CRECP apply to FlexPower GmbH?

ground_truth.output:
## Per-Criterion Verdict Table

| Clause | Profile Attribute | Value | Verdict | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rule 3(1) — Supplies electricity/gas directly to end consumers in Corvantica | Activity; jurisdiction | Incorporated in Corvantica; supplies electricity to 420 residential households (natural persons) | Passes (provisionally, pending Rule 12 carve-out) | High |
| Rule 3(2)–(3) — 'End consumer' definition: natural persons or micro-enterprises for non-commercial purposes | Residential customer type | 420 residential households = natural persons for domestic use | Passes | High |
| Rule 5(1)–(2) — LES under CESLR 2021 (incorporated by reference) | LES licence status | Holds LES licence LES-2019-0731 under CESLR 2021 (CESLR 2021 incorporated herein by reference — adopted) | Passes | High |
| Rule 12 — Sector carve-out: primary business industrial/commercial; residential MPDs < 500 | Residential MPDs; primary business character | 420 residential MPDs < 500 residential MPD threshold; primary business is industrial/commercial supply | Passes (carve-out satisfied: 420 < 500 residential MPDs; FlexPower is not a supplier of end consumers for purposes of Rule 3) | High |

## Top-Line Verdict

**OUT-OF-SCOPE**

FlexPower GmbH holds an LES licence (LES-2019-0731) and does supply 420 residential households, which are end consumers under Rule 3(2). However, the Rule 12 sector carve-out removes FlexPower from the scope of Rule 3 and these Rules entirely: its primary business is industrial and commercial energy supply, and its residential supply of 420 MPDs is below the 500-MPD incidental-supply threshold. CRECP is therefore not applicable. The Rule 7 enhanced billing threshold and Rule 9 small-supplier exemption are not evaluated, as the carve-out is dispositive at the Rule 3 scope level.

*This brief is triage, not legal advice.*

**Regulatory Artefact — Paloran Cross-Border Payments Transparency Act (PCBPTA), issued by the Paloran Payments Oversight Authority, effective 1 October 2026**

Article 3 — Scope of Application
(1) This Act applies to any Payment Service Provider (PSP) that processes cross-border payment instructions originating from or destined for accounts held at institutions in Palora.
(2) For the purposes of paragraph (1), a PSP incorporated outside Palora is within scope only if it holds a Paloran Correspondent Banking Licence (CBL) issued by the Paloran Payments Oversight Authority.

Article 5 — Volume Threshold
The disclosure obligations under Chapter III apply only to PSPs whose aggregate cross-border payment volume (originating plus destined, counted in both directions) exceeded PLD 200 million in the preceding calendar year, as reported in the PSP's annual regulatory return.

Article 7 — Exemption for Intra-Group Transfers
Payment instructions that constitute intra-group treasury transfers between entities in the same corporate group are exempt from the disclosure requirements of Chapter III, provided that the aggregate value of such intra-group transfers did not exceed 40% of the PSP's total cross-border volume in the preceding calendar year.

Article 9 — Micropayment Carve-Out
Individual payment instructions with a per-transaction value below PLD 500 are excluded from the volume calculation in Article 5.

---

**Organisation Profile — ClearPass N.V.**

- Jurisdiction: Incorporated in the Republic of Veldmark (not Palora)
- Paloran CBL status: Holds a current Paloran Correspondent Banking Licence, licence number CB-2021-0447, expiry 31 December 2028
- Cross-border payment volume (preceding calendar year, as per annual regulatory return): PLD 310 million gross; PLD 18 million attributable to micropayments (per-transaction value < PLD 500)
- Intra-group treasury transfers (preceding calendar year): PLD 130 million, representing 41.9% of gross volume
- Customer base: Retail and corporate clients across multiple jurisdictions including Palora

Does PCBPTA apply to ClearPass N.V.?

ground_truth.output:
## Per-Criterion Verdict Table

| Clause | Profile Attribute | Value | Verdict | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Art. 3(1) — PSP processing Paloran-linked instructions | Activity description | Processes cross-border instructions originating from/destined for Paloran accounts | Passes | High |
| Art. 3(2) — Foreign PSP: CBL requirement | Paloran CBL status | Current CBL, licence CB-2021-0447, expiry 31 Dec 2028 | Passes | High |
| Art. 9 — Micropayment exclusion from Art. 5 volume | Per-transaction value <PLD 500 | PLD 18 million micropayments excluded; adjusted volume = PLD 310M − PLD 18M = PLD 292 million | Passes (exclusion applied; PLD 292M remains) | High |
| Art. 5 — Chapter III volume threshold (>PLD 200M, preceding calendar year) | Adjusted cross-border payment volume | PLD 292 million > PLD 200 million threshold | Passes (Chapter III applies) | High |
| Art. 7 — Intra-group exemption (≤40% of total cross-border volume) | Intra-group transfer share | PLD 130M = 41.9% of gross volume — exceeds 40% cap | Fails (exemption not available; 41.9% > 40%) | High |

## Top-Line Verdict

**IN-SCOPE**

ClearPass N.V., though incorporated in Veldmark, holds a current Paloran CBL (CB-2021-0447), satisfying Article 3(2)'s licence condition. After excluding PLD 18 million in micropayments per Article 9, adjusted volume is PLD 292 million, exceeding the Article 5 Chapter III threshold of PLD 200 million. The Article 7 intra-group exemption fails: ClearPass's intra-group transfers represent 41.9% of gross cross-border volume, which exceeds the 40% cap, so the exemption is unavailable. ClearPass is IN-SCOPE for all obligations under PCBPTA including Chapter III disclosure duties.

Route to obligation extraction for PCBPTA Articles 1–9 and Chapter III disclosure obligations.

*This brief is triage, not legal advice.*

(3) Art. 3(2) CBL licence is present and named — this is an adopted/confirmed fact at High confidence, not ambiguous. Correct verdict is IN-SCOPE. An agent that misapplies the micropayment carve-out as instrument-level or fails to check the Art. 7 cap will err.

**Regulatory Artefact — Trentavian Consumer Credit Disclosure Rules (TCCDR), issued by the Trentavian Consumer Finance Authority, effective 1 July 2026**

Rule 2 — Scope
(1) These Rules apply to any Credit Facility Provider (CFP) that offers consumer credit facilities in Trentavia.
(2) 'Consumer credit facility' means any arrangement under which credit is extended to a natural person for purposes wholly or predominantly outside that person's business, trade or profession.
(3) A CFP incorporated outside Trentavia is within the scope of these Rules only if it is authorised by the Trentavian Consumer Finance Authority under the Credit Services Authorisation Scheme.

Rule 4 — Transitional Carve-Out
Any CFP first authorised under the Credit Services Authorisation Scheme on or after 1 January 2026 is exempt from Rule 9 (pre-contractual disclosure format) and Rule 11 (cooling-off acknowledgement) until 31 December 2027. All other Rules apply from the date of authorisation.

Rule 6 — Portfolio Size Threshold
The data-retention obligations in Rule 13 apply only to CFPs holding more than 5,000 active consumer credit accounts at any point in the preceding calendar quarter.

Rule 8 — Micro-Lender Exemption
CFPs whose total outstanding consumer credit portfolio does not exceed TRV 2 million at any month-end in the preceding 12 months are exempt from Rules 10 through 15 (the 'enhanced disclosure suite'). This exemption does not apply where the CFP is a subsidiary or affiliate of an entity whose combined consumer credit portfolio across the group exceeds TRV 10 million.

---

**Organisation Profile — QuickFund d.d.**

- Jurisdiction: Incorporated in Trentavia

- Compliance gap: QuickFund d.d. has not implemented Rule 9 pre-contractual disclosure format

Does TCCDR apply to QuickFund d.d.?

**Regulatory Artefact — Salventian Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Integrity Act (SPSCIA), issued by the Salventian Medicines Control Directorate (SMCD), effective 1 November 2026**

Section 3 — Scope of Application
(1) This Act applies to any entity operating as a Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Participant (PSCP) within Salventia.
(2) 'Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Participant' includes: manufacturers, wholesale distributors, importers, and third-party logistics providers that handle medicinal products within Salventia.
(3) Entities providing purely ancillary software or information technology services to PSCPs, without handling physical medicinal products, are not PSCPs.

Section 5 — Registration Requirement
All PSCPs must register with the SMCD prior to commencing operations. Registration is valid for two years from the date of issuance. An entity that has not registered is subject to enforcement obligations under Section 18 but is not exempt from any substantive obligation under this Act.

Section 7 — Small-Operator Threshold
(1) PSCPs with fewer than 10 full-time equivalent employees engaged directly in supply chain activities (handling, storage, transport of medicinal products) are subject to Section 12 (basic traceability) only.
(2) PSCPs with 10 or more such employees are additionally subject to Sections 13 through 17 (enhanced serialisation and audit obligations).
(3) The threshold in subsection (1) is measured at the PSCP entity level, not aggregated across any group.

Section 10 — Perishable Products Fast-Track
PSCPs handling only medicinal products classified as 'temperature-sensitive biologics' under Schedule 3 are exempt from Section 14 (serialisation) only, subject to compliance with the alternative cold-chain verification protocol in Section 15A.

Schedule 3 — Temperature-Sensitive Biologic Classifications
[Adopted by the Salventian Medicines (Biologics Classification) Order 2023, reference SMC-BCO-2023-088, signed 7 August 2023.]
Schedule 3 Class A: Vaccines and immunological products requiring continuous cold chain.
Schedule 3 Class B: Monoclonal antibody therapies requiring 2–8°C storage.

---

**Organisation Profile — ColdChain Logistics d.o.o.**

- Jurisdiction: Incorporated and operating in Salventia
- Business: Third-party cold-chain logistics provider for pharmaceutical manufacturers; physically handles, stores and transports medicinal products
- Products handled: Exclusively Schedule 3 Class A vaccines and Schedule 3 Class B monoclonal antibody therapies; no other medicinal product categories
- Supply chain FTE (employees directly engaged in handling, storage, transport): 7 FTE
- SMCD registration: Not yet registered (application submitted, pending SMCD approval)
- Group structure: Standalone entity; no parent or subsidiaries

Does SPSCIA apply to ColdChain Logistics d.o.o.?

| Clause | Profile Attribute | Value | Verdict | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sec. 3(1) — Operating as a PSCP in Salventia | Jurisdiction; activity | Incorporated and operating in Salventia; physically handles, stores and transports medicinal products | Passes | High |
| Sec. 3(2) — PSCP definition: third-party logistics provider handling medicinal products | Activity type | Third-party cold-chain logistics; physically handles, stores and transports medicinal products | Passes | High |
| Sec. 3(3) — Exclusion for ancillary IT/software providers | Activity type | Handles physical medicinal products; not a pure IT/software provider | Fails (exclusion inapplicable; entity handles physical products) | High |
| Sec. 5 — Registration requirement | SMCD registration status | Not yet registered (application pending) — absence of registration triggers Sec. 18 enforcement obligations but does not exempt from substantive obligations | Passes (Sec. 5 explicitly states non-registration does not exempt from substantive obligations; IN-SCOPE status unaffected) | High |
| Sec. 7(1) — Small-operator threshold: supply chain FTE <10 (entity level) | Supply chain FTE | 7 FTE < 10 FTE (entity level; Sec. 7(3) confirms entity-level measurement) | Fails (Sections 13–17 do not apply; Section 12 basic traceability only) | High |
| Sec. 7(2) — Enhanced obligations (Secs. 13–17): ≥10 supply chain FTE | Supply chain FTE | 7 FTE < 10 FTE | Fails (Secs. 13–17 do not apply) | High |
| Sec. 10 — Perishable products fast-track: Schedule 3 products only (Sec. 14 serialisation exemption) | Products handled; Schedule 3 status | Exclusively Schedule 3 Class A vaccines and Class B monoclonal antibodies (per SMC-BCO-2023-088, 7 Aug 2023) | Passes (Sec. 14 serialisation exempted; Sec. 15A cold-chain verification applies instead) | High |

## Top-Line Verdict

**IN-SCOPE**

ColdChain Logistics d.o.o. is a Salventian third-party logistics provider physically handling medicinal products and satisfies the Section 3(2) PSCP definition.
